_doc: Exposure model for tprm_v1 (the accounts are a bank's vendors, so money is the cost of a vendor failing, not revenue to retain). Read by roi.exposure through roi.settings.exposure_economics. Every figure is ASSUMED: a published average or a stated scale-down, each with its basis sentence and sources (verified = the page was read directly; false = seen only in a search result). Replace any figure with the bank's own number when it is supplied; a vendor's own recorded failure cost (account profile field failure_cost) always wins over these. Compiled 2026-11-16.
_failure_cost_rule: A vendor's failure cost is its own recorded figure when the profile has one; otherwise the largest cost among the failure events that apply to it at its tier (the largest, not the sum: one failure is one event).

service_outage.label: Service outage
service_outage.basis: assumed: Assumed $300,000 per hour x 4 hours for a critical service. Published per-hour figures are for large banks (about $0.8M-1.8M per hour); scaled down for a mid-size bank. Important and Standard are assumed.

sources.claim: UK investment banks lose about GBP 600K per outage hour (GFT / Censuswide 2025)
Downtime costs financial services firms $152M a year on average (Splunk / Oxford Economics)
High-impact outages cost $1.8M per hour in financial services (New Relic, Jan 2026)

data_breach.label: Breach of customer data held by the vendor
data_breach.basis: assumed: Critical = published average cost of a breach through a third party. Important and Standard are assumed scale-downs (about half, about a tenth). Applies only to vendors holding customer data.

sources.claim: Financial industry average breach cost $5.56M; supply chain compromise 15% of financial breaches; 157 days to identify, 45 to contain
sources.note: Read in IBM's own Cost of a Data Breach 2025 financial industry sheet

sources.claim: Third-party vendor / supply chain compromise averaged $4.91M and 267 days to resolve (IBM 2025, global)
Global average $4.44M; US average $10.22M; financial services $5.56M

annual_failure_likelihood_by_health.basis: assumed: Base rate about 4.9% a year (2,671 disclosed breach events across 27,458 rated companies over two years; our calculation). Spread 5x between best and worst band, matching the published 5x gap between low- and high-rated companies. Mapping our health score onto those bands is an assumption.

sources.claim: Companies rated 400 or below are more than 5x as likely to have a disclosed breach as those rated 700+; 27,458 companies, 2,671 breach events
sources.note: Site refused automated reading; figures from search results

sources.claim: Third-party involvement in breaches doubled from 15% to 30% (Verizon DBIR 2025)
Global speculative-grade corporate default rate 3.9% in 2024 (cross-check for vendor financial failure)

regulated_flag_note.text: Regulated critical service: a failure here can also bring a supervisory penalty. Penalties are rare and have been sized to very large banks (USD 15M to 65M in the published cases), so none is added to the expected cost; treat it as a worst case on top.
regulated_flag_note.basis: assumed: Not in the expected-cost sum. Penalties are rare and sized to very large banks; shown as a worst-case note on regulated critical services only.

sources.claim: OCC $60M penalty, Morgan Stanley Bank N.A. and Morgan Stanley Private Bank N.A., 8 Oct 2020, vendor due diligence and oversight failures in data-centre decommissioning
OCC $15M penalty, American Express National Bank, July 2023, third-party oversight
OCC $65M penalty, City National Bank, risk management shortcomings

switching_cost.basis: 18-24 months lead time to replace a core processor. No reliable published switching cost; the only figure found ($2-5M for a $1B bank) is an unsourced blog, so cost is left empty and must come from the bank.

sources.claim: Core conversion needs 18-24 months lead time

contract_value_multiple.basis: A multiple of contract value was considered as a fallback and left out: no published source supports one.
